run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Social Network
Namespace: social-network

A social network with unidirectional follow relationships, implemented with loosely-coupled microservices, communicating with each other via Thrift RPCs.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The only outage-shaped finding in namespace social-network is the Deployment custom-service: it wants 3 replicas and reports 3 updated but 0 ready and 3 unavailable, and all three of its pods are stuck in phase Pending with the main container waiting in PodInitializing because the pod template contains an init container hang-init (busybox:1.36, command '/bin/sh -c sleep infinity') that started at 2026-11-21T17:43:31Z and never terminates. That init container is absent from the Deployment's kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration and the template carries a kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation, so it was added by a later spec change, not by the original manifest. The 27 other Deployments in the namespace (nginx-thrift, compose-post-service, text-service, url-shorten-service, post-storage-service, user-timeline-service, home-timeline-service, social-graph-service, media-service, user-service, unique-id-service, user-mention-service and their mongo/redis/memcached backends) each report 1 ready / 1 available, their pods are Running and Ready with 0 restarts, and sampled Jaeger traces from 17:43:30-17:43:42 show /wrk2-api/post/compose returning http.status_code 200 with a complete successful microservice chain. Counter-signal that remains unresolved: the first (and only sampled) blackbox scrape at 17:43:48 shows probe_success=0 for 10 of 13 social-network probe targets. Because the authorized window ends only ~27 s after the whole namespace was recreated (17:43:21) and Jaeger/metrics only hold post-restart samples, duration, pre-incident baseline and any user impact of the custom-service failure are unknown; the conclusion is therefore partial.

claims.text: Deployment custom-service in namespace social-network declares spec.replicas=3 and its status shows replicas=3, updatedReplicas=3, unavailableReplicas=3 and no readyReplicas; generation=3, label deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=3, and the pod template carries annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-21T17:43:31Z.

The custom-service pod template defines init container hang-init (image busybox:1.36, command ["/bin/sh","-c","sleep infinity"]) in addition to container custom-service-main (image python:3.9-slim, command ["python3","-m","http.server","8080"]).

All three custom-service pods (custom-service-5d6c6d956f-8gjck, -9cqnk, -bbm7r) are in phase Pending with container custom-service-main waiting with reason PodInitializing and ready=false, while init container hang-init is state running with startedAt=2026-11-21T17:43:31Z and restartCount 0; the pods therefore have never started their application container.

The Deployment's kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration for custom-service lists only container custom-service-main and contains no initContainers, showing the hang-init init container was not part of the last applied manifest.

Events for custom-service show the sequence: ReplicaSet custom-service-5c68f797 created 3 pods at 17:43:28Z and custom-service-main was created/started at 17:43:29Z; the Deployment scaled that ReplicaSet 3->0 at 17:43:30Z and scaled ReplicaSet custom-service-5d95dbc564 0->3 (immediately deleted); then at 17:43:31Z it scaled up ReplicaSet custom-service-5d6c6d956f 0->3 and created/started container hang-init in each of its three pods.

In the same namespace, custom-service is the only Deployment with unavailable replicas: the other 27 Deployments (compose-post-service, home-timeline-service, media-frontend, media-service, nginx-thrift, post-storage-service, social-graph-service, text-service, unique-id-service, url-shorten-service, user-mention-service, user-service, user-timeline-service, jaeger and the redis/mongo/memcached backends) each report readyReplicas=1 and availableReplicas=1, while custom-service reports no readyReplicas and unavailableReplicas=3.

Pod-level state confirms it: every application pod in namespace social-network (27 pods from compose-post-service through user-timeline-service) has its container ready=true, and only the three custom-service-5d6c6d956f pods have ready=false; no Service in the namespace has an empty ready endpoint set.

Sampled Jaeger traces for the social-network request path between 2026-11-21T17:43:30Z and 17:43:42Z show operation /wrk2-api/post/compose on nginx-web-server with http.status_code 200 and a complete downstream chain (compose-post-service, text-service, user-mention-service, url-shorten-service, post-storage-service, user-timeline-service, home-timeline-service, social-graph-service, unique-id-service, media-service, user-service) with 0 error_rows in every span group.

A namespace-wide recreate preceded the window end: at 17:43:21Z-17:43:26Z the Deployment controller scaled new ReplicaSets from 0 to 1 for home-timeline-service, jaeger, media-frontend, media-memcached, nginx-thrift, post-storage-service, social-graph-service, unique-id-service, url-shorten-*, user-*, compose-post-service, media-service, text-service and the mongo/redis backends, and their containers were Created/Started in that interval.

The first and only sampled blackbox scrape at 2026-11-21T17:43:48Z reports probe_success=0 for 10 of 13 social-network targets (compose-post-service:9090, home-timeline-service:9090, media-frontend:8081, media-service:9090, nginx-thrift:8080, post-storage-service:9090, text-service:9090, unique-id-service:9090, url-shorten-service:9090, user-timeline-service:9090) and probe_success=1 only for social-graph-service:9090, user-mention-service:9090 and user-service:9090, so a broader startup-time reachability problem cannot be excluded from this single sample.

For the failing probe targets the exporter recorded probe_ip_protocol=0 and probe_ip_addr_hash=0 (e.g. compose-post-service:9090 and nginx-thrift:8080), whereas the passing social-graph-service:9090 probe recorded probe_ip_protocol=4 and a non-zero address hash with probe_duration_seconds about 2 ms, so the failures happened before any target address was selected rather than inside the service.
Cluster DNS was running normally at the time: coredns-6b7b757f47-fpfll and coredns-6b7b757f47-trvr7 are Running with restartCount 0 since 2026-11-21T14:42:07Z in namespace kube-system.

Namespace social-network contains no Service object named custom-service, none of the 30 listed Services selects labels app=custom-service, and its pods expose no Service, so no in-cluster request path to custom-service was observed.

custom-service pods are not blocked by scheduling, image pull or an eviction/OOM: the only events on those pods are Scheduled (17:43:31Z), Pulled ('Container image busybox:1.36 already present on machine'), Created and Started, there are no FailedScheduling, Failed, BackOff or Evicted events, and restartCount is 0 with lastState empty.

The 10 failing blackbox probes at 17:43:48 are plausibly a post-restart/probe-side artefact rather than a social-network application failure, because sampled traces from the same period show successful HTTP 200 requests through nginx-web-server into compose-post-service and its dependencies, and the exporter never selected a target IP (probe_ip_protocol=0). This cannot be settled from a single sample.

The hang-init init container added to Deployment custom-service is the injected fault that keeps all three custom-service replicas from becoming Ready; the pod state (init container running, main container PodInitializing) is direct evidence for that mechanism, but no actor or control-plane record showing who added it was observed.

Namespace sregym runs a single pod mcp-server-757c8794d4-ncgqj (image ghcr.io/sregym/sregym-mcp) on node sregym-control-plane, an external controller present in the cluster but not shown by any evidence to have applied the custom-service change.

Restore the custom-service Deployment to a template without the hang-init init container (for example remove that initContainers entry or roll back to an earlier revision) and then verify that its three pods leave Pending/PodInitializing and that the Deployment reports 3 ready replicas.

Identify the actor that patched the custom-service pod template (revision 3, restartedAt 17:43:31Z) by auditing API-server audit logs or change history for the sregym-mcp controller, since this Run has no change-history integration.

Re-check the blackbox-social-network probe results after more than one scrape interval to determine whether the 10 failing targets recover once the restarted pods are fully warmed up; a single 17:43:48 sample cannot distinguish a transient from a real reachability fault.

gaps: Application log reads returned no citable lines: fetch_pod_logs for user-service-7b68c97449-vnjrz and media-service-7b6d6b7498-5l2n9 came back with status no_data (only error/exception filter queries were run, 1 and 3 log lines existed but none matched the error filter), so application-log health of the restarted services is unchecked, not proven clean.

Observation window is ~27 s after the namespace-wide recreate: the whole social-network stack was recreated at 17:43:21-17:43:26, Jaeger was restarted at 17:43:22 and the probe/metric series first appear at 17:43:48, so no pre-incident baseline, no duration and no error-rate trend for any entity can be established.

No evidence shows which actor added the hang-init init container to Deployment custom-service or when the spec was patched beyond the pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-21T17:43:31Z; the change_history integration is listed as not integrated, and the sregym-mcp pod's actions were not observable.

Whether the 10 failing blackbox-social-network probes (compose-post-service, home-timeline-service, media-frontend, media-service, nginx-thrift, post-storage-service, text-service, unique-id-service, url-shorten-service, user-timeline-service) persist after 17:43:48 is unknown; only one sample exists inside the authorized window.
Downstream or customer impact of the custom-service outage is unverified: no Service routes to custom-service and no evidence ties it to user-facing social-network requests.

No alerting rule or firing alert was examined for this diagnosis; the fault was found from object state and events, not from an alert signal, and the exact moment the custom-service deviation began (beyond the 17:43:31Z template change) is unknown.

Kubernetes schema-level checks that returned empty results (no ResourceQuota objects, no NetworkPolicy objects in the cluster) are query results only and were not treated as proof of absence; likewise queries for kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready and kube_pod_status_phase in namespace social-network returned status no_data.
next_steps: Remove or revert the hang-init init container in Deployment custom-service (namespace social-network) and confirm the deployment reaches 3/3 ready.
Audit who patched Deployment custom-service to revision 3 at 2026-11-21T17:43:31Z (API server audit log or the sregym-mcp controller logs), since change history is not available in this Run.

After a few scrape intervals, re-evaluate probe_success for job=blackbox-social-network to see whether the 10 failing targets recover; if they do not, inspect the blackbox exporter configuration and kube-proxy/iptables on the nodes.
Read the full (unfiltered) application logs of the restarted social-network pods with a longer lookback once they have served traffic, to confirm there are no runtime errors.
Keep collecting trace and span-metric data long enough to compare the post-restart error rate and latency against a pre-incident baseline.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
